$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-RECUR-001 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §10.10 and the RF-RECUR-001 inventory entry. Mixed-source rule. Expresses prior-injury recurrence-handling STRUCTURE only: one or more prior quadriceps/RF injuries trigger collection of recurrence history fields, mark the episode recurrence-relevant, require recurrence-specific exposure and next-day monitoring, and display the population limits of the evidence. Prior injury alone does NOT create a fixed delay, longer monitoring window, higher pain threshold, or mandatory phase hold; any actual progression decision remains capacity- and response-based. Reported fibrosis is not required to activate this rule and does not increase its authority. No diagnosis, recurrence confirmation, recurrence-risk score, dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, RTS, or raw-media interpretation; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-REHAB-001..006, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, or RF-SAF-006. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: Prior injury changes recurrence handling without imposing a universal delay

input_contract.$comment: Trigger and required history fields taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §10.10. Prior-injury source tiers are distinguished; user-reported prior injury is stored with provenance and uncertainty; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: Prior-injury recurrence-handling structure only. Prior injury changes recurrence-aware handling (history collection, recurrence-relevant marking, recurrence-specific exposure + next-day monitoring, population-limit display) but creates no universal delay, fixed setback, fixed timeline, deterministic recurrence-risk score, or automatic severity/phase/loading/exercise/RTS change. No diagnosis, recurrence confirmation, dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-4 (context gate), V3.1-12 (current-capacity & capacity-to-demand gap), V3.1-13 (rehab prescription/scheduling/monitoring). Evidence roles/grades preserved per source: QRF-042 (D2) prior quadriceps/RF injury population-limited history modifier; QRF-041 (D3) usable ONLY when a valid MRI class exists; QRF-043 (D3) reference-only, not decision-driving recurrence-risk authority; QRF-033 and QRF-034 (I1) population-limitation evidence that must NOT become individual recurrence-prediction authority. Per §10.10 trigger: one or more prior quadriceps or RF injuries. Per §10.10 required behavioural change: collect episode count, side/site, recency, prior management, prior return exposure, and previous failure/non-response; mark the episode recurrent or recurrence-relevant; require recurrence-specific exposure and next-day monitoring; display the population limits of the evidence. Per §10.10 no-automatic-slowing preserved exactly: prior injury alone does NOT create a fixed delay, a longer monitoring window, a higher pain threshold, or a mandatory phase hold; any actual progression decision remains capacity- and response-based. Per §10.10 prohibited inference: reported fibrosis is not required to activate this history rule and does not increase its authority. The rule keeps the source tiers distinct (self-reported / externally documented / imaging-confirmed / valid-MRI-classified prior RF injury / current recurrent-episode evidence), stores user-reported prior injury with provenance and uncertainty, never interprets raw media, and never confirms current recurrence, fibrosis, scar, chronic structural pathology, or central-tendon pathology from prior injury alone. Safety-state choice (read §10.10 exactly): §10.10 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the prior-injury recurrence-handling structure is represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy. The rule creates no dosage, selects no exercises or complete exercise plan, generates no complete rehab plan, and produces no return-to-training or return-to-sport decision; prior-injury handling alone is not progression and not readiness. It does not bypass RF-REHAB-001..006, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, or RF-SAF-006, and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, or RF-SEV-005; uncertainty is preserved when prior-injury source quality, MRI-classification, recurrence, report, capacity, schedule, or monitoring evidence is incomplete. Recurrence-handling rule, not a safety rule. No recurrence engine is authored here (deferred to the later recurrence, rehab, field, and readiness objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
